## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14  
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)  
**Maintenance Interval:** 12 months

## SYSTEM STATUS
This maintenance visit recorded a critical deficiency in pump operation that requires immediate professional attention. The effluent pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its rated electrical load, indicating no hydraulic load is being delivered to the discharge line. This condition poses a risk of motor damage from overheating and prevents the system from functioning as designed. All other components measured within normal parameters, but the system cannot operate safely or effectively until the pump discharge path is restored.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The combined solids layer (scum plus sludge) totals 11 inches, representing 22.9% of the tank's fluid volume. This is within the normal operating range and does not indicate a need for pumping at this time.

## PUMP ASSESSMENT
| Parameter | Measured | Nameplate | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amp Draw | 1.6 A | 7.2 A | CRITICAL |
| Load Percentage | 22.2% FLA | -- | CRITICAL - No Load |
| High Water Alarm | Functional | -- | Good |
| Electrical Connections | Sound | -- | Good |

The pump motor is running but delivering no hydraulic load to the discharge line. At 22.2% of full load amperage, the motor is operating in a no-load condition. This indicates one or more of the following: the pump is running dry (no fluid reaching the impeller), the impeller is broken or missing, or the discharge line is severed or disconnected. A motor operating without fluid cooling and without load will overheat and fail rapidly.

## TANK AND FILTER CONDITION
| Component | Condition | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary Tank | Good | Concrete, 1250-gallon capacity |
| Effluent Filter | Good | Cleaned and reseated during this visit; light soiling |
| Liquid Level | At Outlet | Normal operating level |

The effluent filter was cleaned during this maintenance visit and showed only light soiling, indicating normal biological loading. The tank structure is sound and the liquid level is at the outlet, which is the correct operating position for this system type.

## DISPERSAL FIELD
The dispersal field surface was dry with no evidence of breakout, ponding, or saturation during this maintenance visit.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**CRITICAL -- Immediate professional attention required:**
A qualified technician must examine the pump discharge line for disconnection, damage, or blockage. The pump must also be examined for a broken or missing impeller. The no-load condition must be corrected before the system can resume normal operation. Continued operation risks permanent motor damage.

**Routine:**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once the pump discharge path is restored and normal operation is confirmed.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### The Pump Problem
Your pump is running but not moving water. This is a serious condition because the motor is designed to be cooled by the fluid it pumps. Without that cooling, it will overheat and burn out. The problem is almost certainly in the discharge line -- either it is disconnected, blocked, or broken somewhere between the pump and the dispersal field. A qualified technician needs to trace that line and restore the connection. Do not continue to run the pump until this is fixed.

### Tank and Filter
Your tank solids are at a healthy 23 percent of volume. The effluent filter cleaned up easily and showed only light buildup, which is normal. Keep non-biodegradable material out of the system -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease, medications, and harsh chemicals all slow treatment and accelerate solids buildup. Stick to toilet paper and human waste, and use septic-safe household products.

### Next Steps
Once the pump discharge line is repaired and the pump is confirmed to be drawing normal load current, your system should return to normal operation. Schedule your next routine maintenance visit 12 months from the date of repair.
